summary_paragraph: A 70-year-old woman with a history of HFpEF, CAD with prior CABG, hypertension, and restless legs syndrome was admitted for acute dyspnea and chest pain due to heart failure exacerbation. She presented with volume overload, elevated proBNP, and pulmonary edema on imaging, likely triggered by recent diuretic reduction and high salt intake. She was treated with IV furosemide for three days, transitioned to oral furosemide 40 mg daily, and showed clinical improvement with resolved edema and stable vital signs. Chest pain episodes were determined to be non-ischemic, associated with anxiety. Asymptomatic bacteriuria with Enterobacter aerogenes was identified but not treated. Chronic macrocytic anemia and thrombocytopenia were noted, with outpatient workup recommended. She was discharged home with services, with instructions on weight monitoring, sodium restriction, and follow-up.
problems: Acute on chronic diastolic (congestive) heart failure
Hypertensive heart disease with heart failure
Atherosclerotic heart disease of native coronary artery without angina pectoris
